title: Caching Strategies
description: Understand Next.js multi-layer caching including request memoization, data cache, full route cache, and router cache to build blazing fast applications.

data.text: Caching is one of the most powerful features in Next.js. The framework provides multiple layers of caching that work together to reduce server load, speed up page loads, and improve the overall user experience. Understanding how these layers interact helps you make intentional decisions about when data should be fresh and when it can be cached.

Next.js has four main cache layers: request memoization, the data cache, the full route cache, and the client-side router cache. Each layer serves a different purpose and can be configured independently.

Request memoization deduplicates fetch calls within a single render. If the same URL and options appear multiple times in a Server Component tree, Next.js makes only one request and reuses the result. This happens automatically and requires no configuration.

items: Deduplicates identical fetch calls in the same render pass
Works across nested Server Components without extra setup
Memoized results are not shared across different user requests
The memoization cache is cleared after the render completes

data.text: The data cache persists fetch results across user requests and deployments. Once a fetch is cached, subsequent requests read from the cache instead of hitting the external source. This is the layer that makes static and cached dynamic rendering so fast.

data.title: Configuring the fetch data cache
data.content: Revalidating fetch data every 60 seconds with the revalidate option.

data.text: The full route cache stores the rendered HTML and JSON payload for an entire route. When all data fetches in a route are cached, Next.js renders the route at build time or after the first visit and reuses it for every subsequent request until the cache expires. This is what makes static and cached dynamic rendering possible.

items: Static rendering: the entire route is cached at build time
Cached dynamic rendering: the route is cached after the first request
Dynamic rendering: the route is never cached and renders fresh on every request
Route segment config like force-dynamic and force-static control this behavior

data.text: The router cache is a client-side cache that stores prefetched pages and shared layout data in memory. When a user navigates between pages using next/link, Next.js may show the cached page instantly while silently revalidating in the background. This makes navigation feel instant even on dynamic routes.

data.title: Watch Out
data.text: The router cache is in-memory only and is cleared when the user closes the tab. It does not survive page refreshes or new sessions. Do not rely on it for persistent data storage.

Start with the most restrictive cache option that still meets your freshness requirements. Static rendering is the fastest option for content that does not change often. Cached dynamic rendering with revalidation gives you fresh data with caching benefits. Use no-store only for truly real-time data where stale data would cause problems.

data.title: Summary
points: Next.js uses four cache layers: request memoization, data cache, full route cache, and router cache.
Request memoization deduplicates identical fetch calls within a single render.
The data cache persists fetch results across user requests.
The full route cache stores rendered HTML for an entire route.
The router cache stores prefetched pages in client memory for instant navigation.
Choose the most restrictive cache strategy that meets your freshness requirements.
